title: Aurum Alpha notification preference, and the channel-address state it is checked beside
description: standards/058-notifications.md NF5 and NF7. The root shape is one recipient's consent for one category on one channel, as the product stores it and notify.decide reads it. The $defs carry the second thing notify.decide reads: channelAddress, the verification and suppression state a channel address on the identity record (060 AU3, AU4) must carry for this standard's rules to be decidable. Neither shape holds an address value - the address lives on the identity record and is resolved at send time (NF4). schemaVersion 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

channelAddress.description: NF4 and NF7. The state this standard needs of one channel address on the identity record. verified gates optional notifications; suppression is set by a hard bounce (every class) or a complaint (optional only) arriving as a status event, and cleared only by re-verification. in_app has no address and is not represented.

address_id.description: The address's own public id, so a record can reference a previous address (NF6) without copying it.

channel.description: Which channel this address serves. in_app is deliberately absent.

verified.description: NF4. True once the recipient proved control of the address. Optional notifications never go to an unverified address; the verification message itself is transactional.

suppression.description: NF7. Present while the address is suppressed. hard_bounce suppresses every class; complaint suppresses optional only.

provider.description: The adapter whose status event set it.

recipient_id.description: The recipient's user public id (020 IP1).

tenant_id.description: Where preferences are held per tenant membership.

category.description: NF5. A category from the product's declaration. NEVER security: the NF6 floor admits no preference, and a stored row that looked like one would mislead whoever read it.

allowed.description: NF5. Whether this category may reach this recipient on this channel. Absent a row, the category declaration's default applies.

source.description: NF5. How the consent state came to be: the recipient in the product's settings, an RFC 8058 one-click POST, or an administrator acting for them (audited under 080 AE5 where the product's floor says so). Recorded so a dispute about consent is answerable.
